# FFmpeg test fixtures and native references

Every file here except this README and `manifest.json` is generated by
`../reference/generate-fixtures.sh` using **native FFmpeg n9.0** built by
`../reference/build-native-ffmpeg.sh` from the same pinned tarball as the
Kandelo package (sha256
`7f607a00dd0d28a729d5a4811205812eef01cf6ef6155025febb6f36a9062d52`, signed by
the FFmpeg release signing key `FCF986EA15E6E293A5644F10B4322F04D67658D8`).
The native build uses FFmpeg's portable C code only (`--disable-asm`) and
`-ffp-contract=off`, so neither hand-written arm64 assembly nor fused
multiply-add rounding makes the reference differ from the code Kandelo
compiles. With NEON enabled, native n9.0 decodes and encodes this MPEG-4
Part 2 clip differently from its own C code from the second GOP on — even
with `-flags +bitexact` on the input — while `-cpuflags 0` matches the C
build and Kandelo exactly. (Big Buck Bunny's H.264/AAC hashes are the same
either way.)

Kandelo's `ffmpeg` must reproduce these outputs. FFmpeg's decoders are
bit-exact, so video is compared byte for byte. Both AAC decoders — the
fixed-point one included — are compared per sample within 2, the tolerance
FFmpeg's own FATE tests use for them (`tests/fate/aac.mak`: `CMP = oneoff`,
`FUZZ = 2`): tables built at startup with the C math library legitimately
differ in the last bit between libms. Over Big Buck Bunny's whole
soundtrack, 89 of 57,237,504 samples differ from native, each by 1.

`manifest.json` records the sha256 of every file; `fixtures-manifest.test.ts`
checks it.

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `fixture.mp4` | 2 s, 176x144, 10 fps MPEG-4 Part 2 (with B-frames) + 22.05 kHz mono AAC; `+faststart` so it can be read from a pipe |
| `fixture.ffprobe.json` | `ffprobe` stream summary of `fixture.mp4` |
| `fixture.video.framecrc` | per-frame CRCs of the decoded video |
| `fixture.audio-fixed.s16le` | raw PCM from the fixed-point `aac_fixed` decoder |
| `fixture.audio-float.s16le` | raw PCM from the default (float) `aac` decoder |
| `fixture.browser-encode.framecrc` | packet CRCs of encoding the fixture's video from `testsrc` (the browser test re-encodes in-machine) |
| `bbb.video.streamhash` | SHA-256 of Big Buck Bunny's whole decoded video |
| `bbb.audio-fixed.bytes` | length in bytes of its whole soundtrack decoded by `aac_fixed` to s16le |
| `bbb.audio-fixed.10s-11s.s16le` | native `aac_fixed` PCM for 10–11 s, which contains the first samples that differ |
| `bbb.seek300.framecrc` | 5 frames decoded after `-ss 300` |

## Commands

The exact commands are in `../reference/generate-fixtures.sh`; the tests run
the same argument lists against Kandelo's programs. Change both together.

## Native behaviors

Measured with native n9.0 on 2026-09-26; the process-runtime tests expect the
same from Kandelo.

- **Refusing to overwrite without `-y`**, stdin not a terminal (`-nostdin` or
  stdin from `/dev/null`): prints `File '…' already exists. Exiting.` (or
  `Overwrite? [y/N] Not overwriting - exiting` without `-nostdin`), leaves the
  file untouched, and **exits with status 0**.
- **SIGINT during a long encode** (`-f lavfi -i testsrc=size=320x240:rate=25
  -c:v mpeg4 out.mp4`): exits with status **255** and leaves a valid MP4 whose
  `ffprobe` duration is positive.
